subject: Discovery Recap: FinBot — Inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finbot.ai>, Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@finbot.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: FinBot — Inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Samir / Jane — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Inference unit economics: per-request/token cost is the primary blocker for wider rollout. You cited ~2–3x higher than target at your current scale.
- Latency sensitivity: product needs ~200ms P95 for interactive flows (some async batch is OK for reporting).
- Variable request size: heavy tail of long prompts causing inconsistent batching efficiency.
- Ops overhead: manual capacity tuning and warm-up times leading to degraded experience during spikes.

Current stack / constraints
- Models: proprietary LLMs fine-tuned on customer data (on-premise models + some hosted variants).
- Infra: EC2/GPU clusters (mixed instance types), in-house inference stack with basic batching.
- Compliance: data sensitivity requires audit logs and customer data segmentation for production tenants.

Success criteria (what would make this a go)
- >=40–50% reduction in per-token inference cost at production scale without dropping quality more than ~1–2% on your eval set.
- Maintain <=200ms P95 for interactive routes.
- Reliable autoscaling and predictable cost model for forecast/budgeting.

What FinBot said you were open to
- Trying int8/quantized variants if quality delta is acceptable.
- Exploring prefix/KV caching for repeated user contexts.
- Willing to run a 4–6 week POC if Redwood can demonstrate clear cost/latency wins.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (SE-led) — Rishi from our team to run a model/infra-level assessment and propose a POC scope. Suggested slots: Wed 3/4 10–11am PT or Thu 3/5 2–3pm PT. Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-finbot-tech-deepdive
2) Share sample traffic (anonymized): FinBot to send 24–72 hours of representative requests + token distributions and current cost baseline (attached sample schema).
3) Redwood to return: initial cost model and MAP (attached FinBot_MAP_v1.pdf) + proposed POC milestones.
4) If agreed, Redwood provides a short-term pricing proposal for the POC and runs the performance tests.

Attachments: 20260302-call-recording.mp3 (call recording), FinBot_MAP_v1.pdf, FinBot_sample_traffic_schema.csv

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Rishi on the deep-dive availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Target: our execs are focused on a 50% reduction in token cost vs today to justify moving off the current setup. The current baseline is ~\$1.8 per 1k tokens (after infra + SRE overhead).
- Quantization: we're open to int8/quantization but need to validate on our fraud-detection prompts — even small accuracy drops are risky.
- Traffic: we can provide a 72h anonymized sample and the token distribution CSV you attached.
- Budget: for the POC, we have a discretionary budget for tooling but will need a clear biz case to get larger procurement approval.

Would like Rishi to help us understand risk/expected quality delta for quantized paths and also how Redwood handles fallback to higher-precision models (if quality regresses).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Quick SE assessment notes — FinBot POC prep

Marissa / Vivek — internal note after reviewing the call recording and the sample schema. High level thoughts: 

- Batching: we should prioritize workload-aware dynamic batching to reduce per-token overhead. With the long-tail prompts they described, a combination of small- and medium-window batching plus request prioritization should buy ~20–30% on cost before touching model precision.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching looks promising for their frequent repeated contexts — expect another ~10–15% improvement depending on cache hit rate. Needs TTL/eviction tuning and integration with FinBot's session IDs.
- Quantization: int8 path is feasible; I estimate a conservative 10–25% additional cost reduction but we must run the eval set for accuracy regressions. We should plan an automatic fallback to FP16 for prompts that exceed a regression threshold.
- Risk: primary risk is quality regression on fraud prompts. We should request an eval slice specifically for high-risk intents and set strict pass/fail criteria before enabling quantized path in prod.

Next steps for SE workstream
1) Request anonymized eval slice for fraud detection prompts + acceptance criteria from FinBot.
2) Stand up a short-run harness on Redwood test cluster; run baseline and batched runs.
3) Run quantization experiments and produce a small report with cost/accuracy tradeoffs.

I'll draft a short tech checklist and send to Marissa to include in the POC SOW.


Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
